summary: Grace Tolentino is a 45-year-old chemistry teacher in her 17th year at Alcaraz Flats High, teaching five sections including Dulce Henríquez's third period, sharing lab room B12 with Dana Whitfield. At the start of the fall 2025 semester she is juggling Principal Ocampo's new weekly chronic-absence reports, a lab budget that never stretches, and her daughter Isabel's junior-year college push toward out-of-state engineering schools she fears the family cannot afford. Her mother Corazón lives in the back bedroom, and Grace quietly manages her care, her Sunday Mass and her pharmacy runs. Her husband Ramón works 24-hour dispatch shifts, so most weeknight logistics fall to her. She wants to be a fair, exacting teacher and a good daughter, and she wants Isabel close enough to come home for Sunday sinigang. Money worries, a broken-down minivan, and a department chemistry-lab safety audit press on her through the fall. She uses an assistant weekly, mostly on Sunday evenings after grading, to draft parent emails, rework labs, and sort household logistics.

impressions.statement: Holds her own daughter to a stricter, colder standard than she holds any of her students.

evidence.description: Asks for help writing a gentle, encouraging note to a struggling third-period student, then in the same chat asks for a 'firm list of rules' to tape to Isabel's door about phone use after 11.
Gives a student a lab extension without question but wants the assistant to confirm that Isabel missing an essay draft deadline 'shows a pattern'.
Rewrites a parent email three times to soften it, but sends Isabel a one-line text 'Dishes. Now.' and asks the assistant whether that was too harsh only after Isabel stops talking to her.
Plans conference talking points praising students' effort, then complains Isabel's 4.1 'isn't the point if she can't manage her time'.

impressions.statement: Talks about money in terms of fear of the worst case, even when the numbers are fine.

evidence.description: Asks for a tuition comparison and immediately adds a column for 'if Ramón gets hurt' and 'if Nanay needs a care facility'.
When the minivan dies she asks for the cheapest possible car and dismisses a reliable option $1,800 more as 'reckless'.
Builds a holiday budget then asks whether to skip Thanksgiving extras in case the furnace goes.
Agrees to a higher college cap only after asking for a month-by-month cash projection through 2030.

impressions.statement: Carries her mother's care as an unspoken private duty she won't share with Ramón.

evidence.description: Asks for help reorganizing Corazón's pill organizer schedule at 10 p.m., noting she'll do it before Ramón gets home so he 'doesn't fuss'.
Wants a script to ask Lola Cora about her meter readings without sounding like she's checking up.
Researches grab rails and installs one herself the day after the slip rather than waiting for Ramón's day off.
Plans Thanksgiving seating so her mother is near the bathroom without saying why to the guests.

impressions.statement: Softens on Isabel's out-of-state dream only when evidence, not argument, is in front of her.

evidence.description: Shuts down a conversation about a Colorado school by citing a sticker price.
After Isabel's counselor meeting, asks the assistant to explain net price calculators and seems surprised by the aid numbers.
Loosens curfew after Isabel shows her a written plan with location check-ins.
Raises the budget cap after running three net-price estimates herself.

impressions.changed_to: Starts treating Isabel's far-away college plan as a negotiable project rather than a fantasy.

impressions.statement: Wants precise, numbered steps and gets impatient with hedging or long preambles.

evidence.description: Replies 'just the steps please' when the assistant explains why a lab procedure works before listing it.
Asks for spreadsheet formulas and pastes back the one cell that failed with only 'fix'.
Asks to cut a parent email to under 120 words and to remove 'I hope this finds you well'.
Requests conference talking points 'as bullets, three per kid, no fluff'.

impressions.statement: Grace is checked out and phoning in her teaching this year.

evidence.description: Drops Science Olympiad advising and asks for a quick, reusable worksheet for a week, which looks like coasting but is because the van and her mother's care ate her afternoons.
Spends a Sunday redesigning a density lab so it costs under $40 for all five sections.
Prepares a full inquiry lab on flame tests for Patricia's observation and asks for three differentiation tweaks.
Builds a mole-concept review game for third period because quiz scores dipped, staying up past 11.

impressions.statement: Bristles at administrative paperwork but complies meticulously, then vents sideways.

evidence.description: Asks for help making the absence form faster while muttering about 'forms for the forms'.
Builds a template so exact it auto-flags three-absence students, then sends it to Dana but not to the principal.
Prepares a color-coded chemical inventory for the audit days ahead of time, then complains that no one will read it.
Fills in the required conference logs early but asks the assistant to rephrase a comment so it doesn't sound 'snippy toward the office'.

voice.texting_style: Proper capitalization and full punctuation, like a lab handout; short declarative sentences; occasional 'Ay' or 'naku'; no emoji except a rare thumbs-up; few typos except autocorrected Tagalog words.
voice.with_assistant: Gives just enough context, often pastes rubrics, parent emails or gradebook rows; says please once at the start, then turns brisk; asks for bullets or numbered steps and cuts off long answers with 'shorter'.
quirks: Calls her mother 'Nanay' and 'Lola Cora' interchangeably
Asks for word counts on every email draft
Checks chemistry facts the assistant gives against her own memory and corrects units
Signs off with 'Salamat.' even to the assistant
sample_lines: Please rewrite this parent email under 120 words. Firm but kind. Pasting below.
1) What's a cheap substitute for copper sulfate in a 30-student lab? 2) Safety notes. Bullets.
Shorter. I have five sections and one prep.
Ay. The formula returns #REF again. Here is the cell.
Give me three warm-up questions on significant figures, regular chem level, answers separate.
Naku, no. Moles, not grams. Redo it.
Make a weekly dinner plan for 4 adults, one diabetic-friendly, under $120. Salamat.
